input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: Order Forms auto-renew for twelve months, but exit requires 180 days' advance notice — longer than the 90-day walk-away threshold and well beyond the 60-day fallback window. We therefore shortened the notice window to 60 days, landing the clause at the fallback. The renewal term (twelve months) and the pricing limb in 8.3 (lesser of CPI and three percent) already satisfy the checklist, so pricing is not flagged; we note only that the preferred 30-day opt-out and 60-day Vendor renewal reminder are absent, which we do not press at the fallback target.

ops.oldText: one hundred eighty days' advance written notice

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A 180-day non-renewal notice window is beyond our walk-away threshold, so we have shortened it to 60 days, which is our fallback position (preferred is 30 days with a Vendor renewal reminder). The renewal term of twelve months and the CPI/3% uplift cap in 8.3 are already acceptable.
proposal.summary: Shorten Order Form non-renewal notice window from 180 days to 60 days

mappings.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
mappings.quote: On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent.
